poolGuide.title: Pool guidance
poolGuide.caption: Plan address pools without touching your hosts. Coaming explains the steps and gives you commands to copy. It never runs them.
poolGuide.note: Coaming never runs swarm init or swarm leave, and never edits daemon.json. Run the commands yourself on the right host.

newSwarm.intro: The address pool is fixed when a swarm is created, so decide it now.
newSwarm.avoidHelper: Your LAN, VPN and other sites' ranges.
newSwarm.networksInvalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to {{max}}.
newSwarm.nodesInvalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to {{max}}.
newSwarm.avoidInvalid: Enter a CIDR like 192.168.0.0/16 on each line.
newSwarm.noFit: No range outside the ones you listed is big enough. Remove a range to avoid, or use a smaller subnet size.
newSwarm.summary: This pool holds {{capacity}} networks of /{{mask}}, so {{expected}} networks leave {{spare}} spare.
newSwarm.tooSmall: A /{{mask}} holds {{usable}} addresses, fewer than the {{nodes}} nodes each overlay gives an address to. Choose a bigger subnet size.
newSwarm.commandCaption: Run this on the first manager
newSwarm.fixed: The pool is fixed at init. Changing it later means rebuilding the swarm.

freeSpace.intro: Try these before you rebuild anything. They give space back without downtime.
freeSpace.loadFailed: Couldn't read the address space. Reload the page to try again.
freeSpace.emptyBody: No orphaned networks, and no network is filling up. Small stack subnets are the next thing to turn on.

orphans.title: Remove orphaned networks
orphans.body: {{orphaned}} orphaned and {{unused}} unused networks hold {{addresses}} addresses.

subnets.title: Use smaller subnets for new stack networks
subnets.body: New networks get a /{{mask}} instead of a /24 and the pool lasts about {{times}} times longer.

crowded.title: Spread crowded networks
crowded.body: A network near its limit can run out of addresses during an update. Move some services to a second network.

rebuild.intro: Docker can't change a swarm's pool in place. The only way is to rebuild it.
rebuild.downtime: This means downtime. Every service stops while you rebuild the swarm.

captions.firstManager: Run on the new first manager

backup.title: Back up
backup.body: Back up Coaming's data and anything the stacks keep in volumes.

remove.title: Remove the stacks
remove.body: Remove each stack from Coaming's Stacks page, or run the command below on a manager.
remove.bodyPlain: Remove each stack from Coaming's Stacks page.
remove.skipped_one: {{count}} stack has a name that can't go in a command. Remove it from Coaming's Stacks page.
remove.skipped_other: {{count}} stacks have names that can't go in a command. Remove them from Coaming's Stacks page.

leave.title: Leave the swarm
leave.body: Run this on every worker, then on every manager.

create.title: Create the swarm with the new pool
create.body: The command follows the fields on this tab.
create.waiting: Fix the fields above to see the command.

rejoin.title: Rejoin the nodes
rejoin.body: Get the join token on the manager, then run the join command on each node.

adopt.title: Adopt the new swarm in Coaming
adopt.body: Coaming sees a new cluster. Open this environment's settings and choose Adopt new cluster.

redeploy.title: Redeploy
redeploy.body: Deploy the stacks again from Coaming. Turn on small stack subnets first if you want them.

standalone.intro: Standalone Docker hosts use up their default address pool after about 30 networks. Set your own pools in daemon.json.
standalone.incomplete: Fill in the base and size of every pool to see the snippet.
standalone.restart: Restart the Docker daemon to apply it: sudo systemctl restart docker. Existing networks keep their subnets. Containers stop during the restart unless live-restore is on.
standalone.followUp: Enter the same pools in this environment's settings so Coaming measures against them.
